observations: Two Iveco Eurocargo engines shown in photos 0 and 1.
The engines are heavily soiled, dusty, and have significant red paint peeling.
The engine in photo 0 shows a large air intake manifold and a water pump pulley.
The engine in photo 1 shows a long exhaust manifold and a fuel injection pump.
The engines appear to be used scrap or parts, not new.
No brand or model name is legible on the engine in any photo.
No technical specification plate is visible.

claims.claim: The Iveco Eurocargo is primarily powered by Tector 5 and Tector 7 diesel engines
claims.evidence: The engine in photo 0 shows a Tector 5-style intake manifold, but the engine in photo 1 shows a Tector 7-style exhaust manifold, and the engine in photo 0 is not clearly identified.

risks.risk: The engine may not run or may have seized internal parts.
risks.proof: A video of the engine running or a photo of the engine cranked over.

risks.risk: The engine may be a different model than the seller claims (e.g., Tector 5 vs Tector 7).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine's identification plate showing the model number.

risks.risk: The engine may be a used scrap engine rather than a functional unit.
risks.proof: A photo of the engine with a handwritten note showing the date it was last worked on.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the engine's identification plate showing the model number.
Video of the engine running or a photo of it cranked over.
Photo of the engine with a handwritten note showing the date it was last worked on.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
